title: Frozen Bulk 215nm with Inner Interface Optimization Only
scientific_hypothesis: The high score (0.9227) from round 1 is primarily determined by the bulk cavity region (layers 9-18) converging to ~215 nm uniform thickness. Fixing these layers and optimizing only the transition interfaces (layers 1-8 and 19-20) should maintain score >0.85 with reduced search dimensionality, confirming the bulk cavity as the dominant performance driver.
design_principle: Defective DBR bandpass filter with quarter-wave mirrors and half-wave defect cavity. Bulk cavity thickness fixed at optimal value; only mirror-cavity interfaces optimized for impedance matching.
proposed_topology: 20 explicit layers: Air | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Fused Silica. Layers 1-8 and 19-20 optimizable; layers 9-18 fixed at 215.0 nm.
soft_objectives: minimize mean transmittance in 1400-1500 nm band
minimize mean transmittance in 1600-1700 nm band
manufacturing_considerations: interface layers allow tuning for fabrication tolerance
theory_basis: Defective DBR structure (HL)^N D(LH)^N creates transmission peak at defect wavelength
Quarter-wave optical thickness n*d = lambda0/4 for mirror layers
Half-wave defect cavity n*d = lambda0/2 enables resonant transmission
expected_advantages: Faster convergence with focused search space
known_risks: Interface layers alone may be insufficient to recover round-1 score
Fixed bulk may prevent further improvement if interfaces need co-optimization
execution_request_english: Design a 20-layer Ta2O5/SiO2 bandpass filter on Fused Silica substrate for 1550 nm LiDAR. Layer sequence: alternating Ta2O5/SiO2 starting with Ta2O5. Fix layers 9-18 (indices 8-17, 0-based) at exactly 215.0 nm thickness. Optimize layers 1-8 and 19-20 within bounds [100-400] nm. Incident medium is air. Evaluate transmittance at: passband 1550 nm (single wavelength), stopbands 1400-1500 nm and 1600-1700 nm (spectral means). Objective: maximize passband transmittance while minimizing stopband transmittance. Use gradient-based thickness optimization with coherent plane-wave TMM. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 1400-1500 nm, 1550-1550 nm, 1600-1700 nm. soft objectives: high transmittance at 1550 nm (soft target ≥ 0.95); strong suppression of transmittance in 1400-1500 nm and 1600-1700 nm. behaviors to suppress or avoid: transmittance in 1400-1500 nm; transmittance in 1600-1700 nm. manufacturing constraints: total layers ≤ 30.
revision_reason: Following feedback directive to fix bulk layers 9-18 at optimal ~215 nm values from iteration 21, restricting optimization to interface layers only to verify score maintenance with reduced DOF.
